hook.text: Side one's master tape was left in a London taxi, so most of that side was remixed overnight.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: May to June and October 1967, Olympic Studios, London

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Jimi Hendrix (vocals, electric guitar, piano, recorder), Noel Redding (bass guitars, backing vocals), Mitch Mitchell (drums, backing vocals)

sentences.text: The band finished its debut, Are You Experienced, in late April 1967.
It kept its regular recording schedule and returned on May 4 to start writing songs for a follow-up LP.
The album came out only seven months after the debut's release.
The lyrics of Spanish Castle Magic were inspired by a dance hall near Seattle, where Hendrix jammed with other local bands in high school.
Eddie Kramer and George Chkiantz handled the engineering.
The basic tracks went onto a four-track recorder, with stereo drums on two tracks, bass on a third and rhythm guitar on a fourth.
They mixed that onto a second four-track recorder, leaving two more tracks for lead guitar, vocals and percussion.
Hendrix often asked for many re-takes, and Kramer stayed patient with him.
Hendrix and Mitchell had begun to voice their own views on creative choices that Chandler had handled on the debut.
Chandler had grown tired of the guitarist's perfectionism by October 1967, and Redding began to resent Hendrix's instructions on what he played.
Cat Talking to Me, from that June session, appeared in 2010 on the posthumous album West Coast Seattle Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Anthology.
The Hendrix Estate released a box set called The Jimi Hendrix Experience: Bold As Love Sessions on November 7, 2025.
The 66 tracks include demos and alternate takes, and the Blu-ray adds a Dolby Atmos mix.
Malaysia's Home Ministry banned the album's art after complaints, and some Hindus have since voiced anger over the religious images on the cover.

listen_for.text: It opens with microphonic and harmonic feedback, and sounds from Hendrix's guitar pan across the stereo field to circle the listener.
Hendrix plays recorder on it, and the percussion effect comes from Chandler, Hendrix, Graham Nash and Gary Leeds stomping on a drum riser.
On this track Hendrix first uses a Leslie speaker for his guitar, a revolving speaker that gives a wavering effect.
The song starts on a swirling, backwards guitar solo, and Roy Wood and Trevor Burton of the Move add backing vocals.
Hendrix plays harpsichord on it, and the coda uses stereo phasing for the first time on record.
